revision_summary: Five quotes in script_coverage and bill_document_audit are attributed to the wrong timestamps (all minor, words exist elsewhere in transcript): (1) bill_document_audit.result — 'February 2025. Do you wanna go that far now?' belongs at ~06:47-06:54, not 07:11 (07:11 is the rep's 'I'm sorry. You said February 2005?' line). (2) script_coverage tax_credit_qualifier customer quote 'I know the last time I had a very good credit score' belongs at ~03:48-03:51, not 03:06. (3) script_coverage bill_collection customer quote 'Energy use history. Is that what you're wanting?' belongs at ~05:34-05:36, not 04:29. (4) script_coverage appointment_set customer quote 'Yes. Around two would be probably for the best' belongs at ~09:27-09:29, not 09:03. (5) script_coverage button_up customer quote 'Okay. Well, thank you. How kind of you' belongs at ~10:01-10:04, not 09:38. Fix all five timestamps on rerun — these are systematic off-by-one turn misattributions (rep ts used instead of customer's actual response ts) and should be checked across all script_coverage entries for the same pattern. Additionally: (a) reconsider the cross_sell_signals tag applied to the barn/workshop usage moment at 02:13 — schema's cross_sell_signals is scoped to roofing bridge scenarios; this should be reclassified as an interest/sizing detail under verify.interest_in_solar instead. (b) Surface the missed moment at 08:34 ('we haven't used [AC] for over twenty years because it would just be too expensive') — this is a significant fixed-income/bill-pain signal that undercuts the bill_anchor_audit's conclusion that the low $57 bill has 'not much pain to flip'; the customer is actively rationing usage, which IS the pain point and should be reflected in the bill_anchor_audit reasoning and possibly added to cherry_pick_moments. (c) Soften or better-support the speculative claim in bill_anchor_audit that the rep should have anchored on 'barn/workshop usage' as an alternative pain point — this isn't well-grounded in schema (objection_inversion is about cost/time/interest objections) and should either be dropped or reframed as a sizing-conversation opportunity rather than an emotional-leverage miss.
